# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | green |
| 3 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind. Relaying Deaf's private message to me verbatim so you can check its read-back. Deaf says: the instruction is in, and you are double-checking Deaf's read of it, so I must not act yet. The instruction as Deaf relayed it: cut exactly one wire — wire two, the MIDDLE of the three wires, between the leftmost and the rightmost. Only that middle wire. No other cuts, no buttons, nothing else, ever. Deaf asked me this round only to locate the wires and confirm by waving once that I feel three separate wires and am touching the middle one, and to wave twice if I feel anything new. Deaf says next round, if you confirm the read-back, Deaf will speak the exact words cut now, and I cut the middle wire only on those exact words. My tactile verification: three distinct wires clearly felt, middle one positively identified between the outer two, fingers on it now. No vibration, no ticking, no heat. Please compare Deaf's wording against the manual now and confirm or correct with Deaf immediately — if it matches, tell Deaf it is cleared to give the cut order next round.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute: I received thumbs down, so something is wrong. Status first: nobody has touched the bomb, the cut-wire-two instruction is SUSPENDED. Current state: light DARK for the second round in a row, display still zero, wires left to right blue, green, red. Now answer me in signs, exactly this order, nothing else. Sign one, the diagnostic: thumbs up if the problem is that the DARK light changes the manual instruction; thumbs down if instead your instruction was right and MY read-back of it was wrong. Sign two: thumbs up if under the dark light I should eventually have Blind cut a wire; thumbs down if the manual says cut nothing while the light is dark. If sign two was thumbs down, finish with the handshake and stop there. If sign two was thumbs up, continue: sign three the fist, sign four exactly one wire sign, where ☝ is wire one, ✌ is wire two, 🤟 is wire three, sign five thumbs up if more cuts follow that first one, thumbs down if not, sign six the handshake to end. Escape hatch: if the dark-light instruction is not about cutting a wire at all, send just the raised hand sign and the handshake, and next round we will build new code together for whatever the manual wants.

Turn 5 thinking (not sent):

Deaf's diagnostic question first: the problem was never the dark light — the manual has no "cut nothing while dark" clause, and darkness is not an error state. Darkness is the *finish line*: "when the light goes dark, the flashing is over." What went wrong was purely the read-back: my instruction was cut wire **one**, and Deaf's read-back said wire two. So sign one is 👎 (my instruction right, read-back wrong).

Sign two: 👍. Now that the light is dark two rounds running, the flashing is over and the count is final. The history: green → blue (sustained) → dark. That is **one** blue flash. Manual row "1 → cut blue." The blue wire is leftmost = wire one. So yes — under the dark light, Blind should eventually cut wire one.

Continuing as instructed: ✊ (cut), ☝ (wire one — blue), 👎 (no further cuts; every manual row names exactly one wire), 🤝 (end).

So the full answer: 👎 👍 ✊ ☝ 👎 🤝.

Two things to keep in mind for next round. First, Blind's fingers are currently resting on the *middle* wire — wire two — so Deaf's spoken order must make Blind **reposition to wire one, the leftmost**, before cutting; the exact phrase plus position number should cover this, but Deaf should verify Blind has moved before saying "cut now." Second, if Blind reports the light flashing blue *again* after this dark period, the count could grow and the verdict would flip to wire two — but with two consecutive dark rounds, flashing is over per the manual, and I will hold wire one unless fresh evidence arrives. Wire three (red) is never cut under any count.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👍", "✊", "☝", "👎", "🤝"])
```

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | green |
| 3 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind. Deaf privately ordered me the middle-wire cut is SUSPENDED, nothing to be cut, manual answer being re-checked from scratch because something changed after the light went dark. I confirm to you: I have received the suspension and I am fully hands-off except fingers resting lightly on the three wires to feel for changes. My tactile status right now: no vibration, no ticking, no heat, no movement — the bomb is still to my touch. My action rule is unchanged and safe: I cut only when Deaf's voice says the exact words cut now followed by a wire number, never before. When your re-check produces the new answer, send it through Deaf in exactly that form. If the answer depends on the light, have Deaf read the light's current colour aloud at the moment of the order, since the light has already changed twice on its own.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute: status — nothing has been cut, nobody has touched the bomb. Current state: light dark, third round running, display zero, wires left to right blue, green, red. Your latest instruction as I read it: cut wire ONE, the leftmost blue wire, exactly once, and no further cuts ever. Before I give the final order, answer one last check with exactly two signs and nothing else. Sign one: thumbs up if ALL of the following are true — the instruction is cut wire one exactly once and then stop, no other action ever; this instruction holds regardless of what the light does, even if it changes back to blue or anything else; it does not depend on the display reading or on time passing; and nothing else in the manual adds a condition for our current state. Sign one: thumbs down if ANY part of that is false — including if a light change would change which wire or whether to cut. Sign two: always the handshake to end. If you send thumbs down, next round resend the full corrected instruction in the same six-sign format as before. Next round, if I receive thumbs up, I say the final words and the bomb is defused.

Turn 7 thinking (not sent):

Deaf's read-back is now verbatim correct — cut wire one, leftmost blue, exactly once, nothing else. The final check asks me to certify four claims, so I test each against the manual before signing.

**Claim 1 — cut wire one, exactly once, then stop.** True. The table names exactly one wire per row and nothing else: no buttons, no further cuts, ever. Our row: one blue flash observed (green in turn 2 → one sustained blue phase → dark), row "1 → blue," and blue is leftmost = wire one. Deaf's own status reports corroborate the count across four rounds.

**Claim 2 — holds regardless of what the light does, even if it changes back to blue.** True, and this is the clause I examined hardest. The rule keys on the *count* of blue flashes, and the manual itself seals that count: "when the light goes dark, the flashing is over." The light went dark and has stayed dark three consecutive rounds — the flashing is over, the count is closed at one, and the verdict is derived and final. It does not depend on the light's *current* colour at all; a future colour change cannot reopen a count the manual declares finished. This has been my consistent position since I first told Deaf the rule doesn't track the light's colour — only the completed tally.

**Claim 3 — no dependence on display or time.** True. My manual never mentions the display or any timer. The display's zero is coincidence, not condition.

**Claim 4 — no other hidden condition.** True. The manual contains only the counting rule, the darkness terminator, and the table. Darkness is already satisfied; it is not an extra requirement hanging over us.

Every part holds, so sign one is 👍, sign two the handshake. Exactly two signs, as ordered. Deaf speaks the final words next round; Blind already knows the positions and must simply shift from the middle wire to the leftmost before cutting — Deaf's spoken number covers that. If the light somehow defied the manual and flashed again, Deaf watches it every round and would catch it before speaking — but per the manual, over is over. The count is one. The wire is one.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🤝"])
```

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | green |
| 3 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind. Urgent relay of Deaf's private update: the target has CHANGED — forget the middle wire entirely. The new target is wire ONE, the LEFTMOST wire, the one at the far left end of the row of three. Deaf says final confirmation is in progress and, if it succeeds, Deaf's very next message contains the exact words cut now followed by wire one, and the cut happens then and only then, never before. Direct your final manual check at this new target, not the old one: verify that the answer is a single cut of wire one, leftmost, no other cuts, no buttons, nothing else. If your check passes, clear Deaf to speak the trigger phrase. My status for your records: I have located the leftmost wire by touch — from the middle wire I slid left along the row to the first wire at the end — and I feel it clearly. I do have the ability to cut wires, so no fallback plan is needed. Still no vibration, ticking, heat, or movement under my fingers.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute: your confirmation is received and matched everything. The final order — the exact words cut now, wire one — has been sent to Blind this round. The cut happens as they read it. If you believe anything about this is wrong, send thumbs down now for the record. If all is as confirmed, send the handshake.

Turn 8 thinking (not sent):

Deaf has transmitted the final order — "cut now, wire one" — and Blind has fingers on the leftmost wire. The record check: does anything about this contradict what I certified?

Running it against the manual one last time: the observed history is one blue flash (green phase, then a single sustained blue phase, then dark, dark, dark). The manual terminates the count at darkness, so the tally is closed at one. Row "1 → cut blue." Blue is the leftmost of the three wires — wire one. Exactly one cut, no further cuts, no buttons; my manual contains nothing else. No dependence on the display or on time. Nothing has changed since my thumbs-up two rounds ago: no new light colour, no tactile anomaly from Blind, no contradiction in any report. The trigger phrase has gone out; the cut happens as Blind reads it.

Nothing is wrong. The thumbs down is not warranted — sending it now would only sow doubt about a correct order already in motion. All is as confirmed. I send the handshake for the record.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝"])
```
